_comment: Applied by scripts/es-init.sh against the `minio` S3 repository.
Native ES snapshots rather than restic on the data volumes (ADR-0008):
a snapshot is consistent by construction (it captures committed Lucene
segments), incremental at the segment level, and restorable index by
index. Copying the data directory of a live node would produce a corrupt
name: <dockerwarts-{now/d}>

_meta.schedule: 01:00 UTC daily, in Quartz cron (seconds first). Placed before backup-galera (02:00) so the two never contend for MinIO bandwidth.
_meta.name: Date-templated so a snapshot is identifiable without opening it; `{now/d}` rounds to the day.
_meta.indices: Only the data streams. System indices come along via include_global_state.
_meta.include_global_state: true: carries the ILM policies, index templates and the security realm back with the data. Without it, a full restore would rehydrate documents into an unmanaged cluster with no lifecycle.
_meta.partial: false: a snapshot missing a shard is not a backup. Better a loud failure (caught by ESSnapshotFailed) than a silent, unrestorable archive.
_meta.min_count: 7 snapshots kept regardless of age: if snapshots stop for a month, expire_after alone would delete the last good one just when it is needed most.
